newsitem.title: USA: U.S. panel aims to reduce fatal air accidents.
newsitem.headline: U.S. panel aims to reduce fatal air accidents.

text.p: A White House commission on Wednesday called for an 80 percent reduction in fatal air accidents over the next 10 years.

Vice President Al Gore, speaking at the commission's final meeting, said its key goals were "to dramatically reduce the rate of fatal accidents," as well as to accelerate modernisation of the U.S. air traffic control system and to boost the fight against terrorism.

Gore said the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) would annouce later Wednesday, "in response to our goal to reduce fatal accidents by 80 percent over 10 years," a program of air safety research that would cost $500 million over five years.
The panel also recommended that enhanced ground proximity warning systems should be installed in all commercial and military passenger aircraft.

Gore said this digital display would mean that "never again will an airplane like the one (late Commerce Secretary) Ron Brown was flying on...not have a clear and timely warning to the pilot...that a hill or mountain is ahead." Brown died last year when the military plane in which he was flying crashed into a hillside in Croatia.

The White House commission on aviation and security was formed in response to last year's crash of TWA flight 800 near New York. The commission was expected to hand its recommendations to President Clinton later on Wednesday.
